## Read this first

This app refuses features on purpose. It is a clock for a phone that is looked
at and never operated, so the interface stays naked: at rest nothing is visible
but the clock on black, and every setting hides behind a gesture and fades away
again.

Out of scope, and requests for these will be declined however well they are
argued:

- Timers, alarms and stopwatches
- Weather, calendar and news
- Music or media control
- Accounts, sync and anything that needs a backend
- A color picker. Themes are curated presets only.
- Any permanently visible control: a settings gear, a toolbar, a panel, a button

The settings list is exactly five entries and is not growing: 24 hour time,
seconds on/off, date on/off, theme preset, brightness.

New runtime dependencies are also declined unless they solve a problem that
plain SvelteKit genuinely cannot. The dependency count is zero and that is a
feature.
